text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures ended slightly firmer in quiet trade. There were no fresh fundamental news to influence prices. May ended $1.60 higher at $309.90, while August added $1.10 to close at $308.10. Raw sugar futures in New York settled mostly firmer and at a key chart level basis the May contract, setting the stage for further gains. However, fundamentally there is no reason for prices to show significant gains. May added 6 points to close at 11.03 cents/lb, while July closed 3 points firmer at 10.77 cents/lb. FUNDAMENTALS

TRINIDAD & TOBAGO - Sugar production in 1998 is forecast to reach 128,800 tonnes, raw value, up from 125,300 tonnes expected for 1997 and 115,000 tonnes produced in 1996. Sugar consumption in 1998 will be around 77,000 tonnes, unchanged from 1997 but up on the 1996 figure of 72,000 tonnes.

SOUTH AFRICA - Sugar production in 1996/97 (May/April) is now put at 2.270 million tonnes, tel quel, up from 1.667 million tonnes produced in 1995/96. Consumption in 1996/97 is forecast to rise by 2 per cent from 1.278 to 1.304 million tonnes.

FRANCE - Sugar imports in December 1996 amounted to 37,677 tonnes, raw value, slightly up on the 35,498 tonnes imported in December 1995. This brought cumulative imports in the first quarter of 1996/97 (October/December) to 133,033 tonnes, compared to 123,171 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 476,602 tonnes compared to 364,140 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in October/December 1996 were Reunion with 40,501 tonnes raws compared to 29,904 tonnes, Swaziland with 10,972 tonnes compared to 1 tonne and Guyana with 7,801 tonnes against 8,300.

Sugar exports in December 1996 amounted to 265,029 tonnes against 306,012 tonnes in December 1995. This brought cumulative exports in October/December up to 933,934 tonnes compared to 966,173 tonnes in the corresponding period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 2.896 million tonnes compared to 3.067 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in October/December 1996 were Belgium with 249,769 tonnes whites compared to 292,965 tonnes, Algeria with 125,773 against 42,253 tonnes, Iran with 88,602 compared to 55,300 tonnes and Saudi-Arabia 77,759 against 46,201 tonnes.

UNITED KINGDOM - Sugar imports from third countries in January 1997 reached 96,381 tonnes, raw value, which brought cumulative imports in the first four months of 1996/97 (October/January) up to 403,609 tonnes against 411,416 tonnes in the corresponding period the previous year. Total imports from third countries in 1995/96 amounted to 1.237 million tonnes. Major countries of origin in October/January 1996/97 were Mauritius with 201,052 tonnes raws against 216,570 tonnes, Guyana with 101,643 compared to 65,310 tonnes and Fiji with 79,900 against 85,180 tonnes.

Sugar exports to third countries in January 1997 amounted to 14,977 tonnes which brought cumulative exports in October/January 1996/97 to 67,147 tonnes, down from 79,554 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports to third countries in 1995/96 amounted to 324,415 tonnes. Major countries of destination in October/January 1996/97 were Israel with 25,265 tonnes whites against 25,940 tonnes and Norway with 14,779 compared to 16,434 tonnes.
